title: The Apology — Sc142: Gumball falls apart and reassembles (body-part gag)

source.github: mhvnsnt/cn-gigaleak-gumball, draft release untagged-1676e192ae8c72e95791, asset id 640772406
source.method: FLA (XFL zip) read via sequential local-header parser (2012 Flash zips have malformed central directory); DOMDocument.xml + LIBRARY symbol XMLs parsed directly. Same neutral per-keyframe transform format as production/dance-choreo v1: a part pose is (item, first_frame, affine matrix a/b/c/d/tx/ty, pivot). keyMode 9728 = pose-to-pose; sampled_frames hold each keyframe's elements to the next keyframe, matching SWF playback.

teaches: Transformation by puppet dissection: the joke is staged by breaking the puppet into separately-placed pieces. The scene opens on Gumball's legs walking in ALONE; head, torso and limbs are then placed as independent scene elements on the GB layer, splayed in impossible positions (multiple legs, head too big for the body, parts trailing behind), and the pieces progressively recombine until a strained, teeth-gritted whole Gumball stands at frame 75. No morphing — just per-part placement, scale and timing on a locked hallway background.
notes: Frame 1 is only legs + tail: the scene trusts the audience to read dislocated parts as the character.
The head comp holds 805 keyframes — more than the body puppet (555): the giant gritted-teeth head is the visual anchor while the body is in pieces.
A 'Roughaurel' layer (rough pass by animator Laurel) ships inside the clean file — rough and clean coexist in production files.
Background is a locked school hallway (tile wall, red window frames): all motion is character-side, which makes the part chaos readable.
